WHO THIS IS FOR

Production-style means: documented IPs, HTTPS everywhere internally, separate backup target, monitoring that alerts, and a restore you've actually tested. If it isn't backed up and monitored, it isn't “done.”

1. Reference architecture — one node, done right

Start with one Proxmox node. One node done cleanly beats three nodes done messy, every time. You can add a second node later for clustering / HA — the layout below doesn't paint you into a corner.

EDGERouter → Managed switchYour ISP router (or OPNsense later) → NETGEAR GS108Ev3-class managed switch. VLAN-capable from day one, even if you start flat.
COMPUTEProxmox VE host “sly”Mini PC (OptiPlex 7070 Micro i5-9500T in my lab). SSD for VMs/LXCs. Runs templates, Docker host, DNS, proxy, monitoring.
STORAGE + POWERNAS + UPSQNAP TS-216G-class 2-bay NAS as backup target + shared storage. APC BR1500MS2-class UPS so blips = non-events and shutdowns are clean.

Traffic flow: Devices → switch → Proxmox services (AdGuard for DNS, Nginx Proxy Manager for HTTPS) → Tailscale for remote access. No port-forwards to the internet for admin panels. Ever.

My live proof: This is the same layout behind my Homelab Command Center build log — 11 guests on one node: services LXC (Docker), Portainer agent, networking/DNS, Vaultwarden, Firefly III, WordPress + MariaDB, templates and more.

2. Hardware baseline — spend where it matters

You don't need enterprise gear. You need quiet, low-power, reliable — because this will run 24/7 in your home or office.

PieceMinimum viableWhat I run (steal this)
ComputeMini PC / SFF, 4-core CPU, 16GB RAM (32GB recommended), 512GB SSDDell OptiPlex 7070 Micro · i5-9500T — small, quiet, sips power, ideal first node
Switch8-port managed (VLAN-capable)NETGEAR GS108Ev3 — VLANs without enterprise pricing
Storage / backupExternal drive or NAS, separate from host SSDQNAP TS-216G 2-bay NAS — backup target + shared storage in the 3-2-1 layout
PowerUPS with USB signallingAPC BR1500MS2 — rides out blips, clean shutdown on extended outage. Non-negotiable.
Rack (optional)Small shelf is fine to startRackPath 9U — keeps switch, node, UPS and cables tidy once you grow

Budget order if you're buying piecemeal: UPS first (protects everything), then compute + RAM, then managed switch, then NAS. A pretty rack with no UPS is a liability with good cable management.

3. Proxmox layout — templates, guests, storage

Install & first 30 minutes

  1. Install Proxmox VE from ISO, set a static IP on your management network, and write it down (tape on the box counts as documentation if you also put it in a note).
  2. Switch apt to the no-subscription repo if this is a lab, run full updates, reboot.
  3. Storage: local SSD = local-lvm (LVM-thin) or ZFS for VM disks. Backups never live only on the same disk as the VMs. Add your NAS as NFS/SMB storage for backups.
  4. Set up email / webhook notifications under Datacenter → Notifications so host alerts leave the box.

The golden template (do this before any “real” VM)

  • Install Rocky Linux 9 minimal, apply all updates, install qemu-guest-agent + cloud-init, set your timezone / locale / admin user.
  • Clean machine-id and SSH host keys, then convert to template. Name it like rocky9-golden-2026-10 — future-you will thank present-you.
  • Every Linux VM from now on is a clone of this. Consistent, fast, repeatable — the same habit you'd want in a client environment.

Guest plan (single-node starter)

GuestTypeJob
docker-hostLXC or VMYour Docker services via Portainer. One host to start — don't shard prematurely.
net-servicesLXC / VMAdGuard Home (DNS), Nginx Proxy Manager (reverse proxy + Let's Encrypt).
monitoringLXC (can co-locate early)Uptime Kuma + Homepage dashboard. If it matters, it alerts.
templatesTemplateRocky 9 golden image (+ Ubuntu if you prefer it for Docker).

Resource discipline: give the Docker host the most RAM, keep everything else lean (1–2 vCPU, 1–2GB to start). Proxmox makes resizing easy — undocumented over-provisioning makes troubleshooting miserable.

4. Networking — DNS, VLAN thinking, remote access

  • DNS filtering: AdGuard Home as your network DNS. Point your router's DHCP DNS at it. You get ad/tracker blocking + a query log that will teach you more about your network in a week than a month of guessing.
  • VLAN thinking (even if day-one is flat): Plan three zones — Trusted (your PCs / servers), IoT (TVs, bulbs, cameras), Guest. Implement on the managed switch + router when ready. The plan is free; retrofitting without a plan is not.
  • Remote access: Tailscale on the Proxmox host + key services. It punches through CGNAT, needs no port-forwards, and gives you named, ACL'd access. This replaced VPN pain in my lab entirely.
  • HTTPS everywhere: Nginx Proxy Manager in front of every web UI, with real certs (Let's Encrypt via Cloudflare DNS challenge if you own a domain). vault.yourdomain.com beats 192.168.1.47:8080 in every way that matters.

Document as you go: keep one page (Wiki.js, Notion, even a Markdown file) with: IP plan, guest list, credentials location (Vaultwarden — not a sticky note), backup schedule, restore-test dates. In production, documentation is the system.

5. The starter stack — what to run first

Install in this order. Each piece makes the next one easier.

#ServiceWhy first
1PortainerSee and manage Docker without living in the CLI. You will still learn the CLI — with a safety net.
2Nginx Proxy ManagerOne place for hostnames + SSL. Every later service gets a clean URL on day one.
3AdGuard HomeNetwork DNS + filtering. Immediate quality-of-life win for every device.
4VaultwardenSelf-hosted password vault (Bitwarden-compatible). Your lab credentials need a real home immediately.
5Uptime Kuma + HomepageMonitoring + a dashboard that makes the lab feel like a system, not a pile of tabs.
6One “real” serviceFirefly III, Wiki.js, WordPress — pick the one you'll actually use weekly. Usage is what turns a lab into a skill.

Container rules (production habits, homelab scale)

  • One Compose file per service, named volumes, .env for secrets — never secrets in git.
  • Pin image versions (image: service:1.2.3), update deliberately. “Latest broke at 2am” is a rite of passage you only need once.
  • Every Compose file lives in version control (without secrets). If the host dies, redeploy = clone repo + docker compose up -d.

6. Backups that restore — 3-2-1 or it didn't happen

3 copies, 2 different media, 1 offsite/offline. In this layout: live VMs (copy 1) → NAS via Proxmox backup (copy 2) → offsite / offline copy (copy 3 — cloud bucket or a rotated external drive).

  • Schedule: nightly incremental-friendly backups, retain 7 daily + 4 weekly. Databases (MariaDB etc.) get logical dumps too — VM snapshots alone are not a database backup strategy.
  • Monthly restore test (the whole point): pick one VM, restore it to a test ID, boot it, log in, verify the service. Log the date and result. An untested backup is a hope, not a backup.
  • Config backups: Compose files, Proxmox config notes, router/switch exports. Rebuilding hardware is annoying; rebuilding undocumented config is a lost weekend.

This is also a Sylvect service for a reason: most small businesses I meet “have backups.” Almost none have a dated, successful restore test. If reading this made you nervous about your business systems, that's section 05 below — the Backup & Recovery Check exists for exactly that.

7. Security baseline (30 minutes, huge payoff)

  • Unique admin passwords in Vaultwarden + 2FA on Proxmox and your registrar / Cloudflare.
  • SSH keys, no password SSH on guests; updates on a cadence (weekly lab, planned windows for anything client-facing).
  • No admin UIs exposed to the internet — Tailscale or VPN only. Reverse proxy gets HTTPS + strong auth for anything sensitive.
  • UPS monitored (NUT or vendor tool) so guests shut down cleanly before the battery dies.

8. The weekend build order

DAY 1 — FOUNDATION

Proxmox + template + Docker

  • Install Proxmox, static IP, updates, storage + NAS backup target
  • Build Rocky 9 golden template (updates, guest agent, cloud-init)
  • Clone Docker host, install Docker + Portainer
  • Deploy Nginx Proxy Manager, first hostname + cert working
DAY 2 — SERVICES + SAFETY

DNS, monitoring, backups

  • AdGuard Home live, router DNS pointed at it
  • Tailscale on host + phone, remote login proven
  • Vaultwarden + Uptime Kuma + Homepage up
  • First backup job runs and one restore test passes — then you're done

What to skip for now: Kubernetes, HA clustering, Ceph, a second node “for later,” and any service you can't name a weekly use for. Depth on one node teaches you more than breadth across five half-finished systems.

Common first-month mistakes (so you can skip them)

  • Backups on the same disk as the VMs (that's one copy with extra steps).
  • Port-forwarding Proxmox / Portainer to the internet “temporarily” (it never is).
  • Twelve services, zero monitoring, first alert = a family member saying “the internet is down.”
  • No IP / credential documentation until “later” (later is doing it from memory at midnight).

9. Starter checklist — tap to track your build

Tap items as you complete them. Your progress stays on this device for this visit — enter your email above to get the permanent copy delivered to your inbox.

  • ✓Hardware ready — mini PC (16–32GB RAM), managed switch, UPS on the desk
  • ✓Proxmox installed — static IP, updates done, NAS added as backup storage
  • ✓Golden template built — Rocky 9, guest agent + cloud-init, cloned once successfully
  • ✓Docker host live — Portainer up, NPM issuing real HTTPS certs
  • ✓DNS + remote access — AdGuard serving the network, Tailscale login proven from your phone
  • ✓Core stack up — Vaultwarden, Uptime Kuma, Homepage, one real service you use weekly
  • ✓Backups + restore test — nightly job running, one VM restored and verified, date logged
  • ✓Documented — IP plan, guest list, credential locations and restore dates on one page
